// R3 reached the parent's testing.TB only where it was a name it could
// classify: a parameter, or a var with the type written out. A TB bound by an
// initializer, or reached through a field, produced the same parent-FailNow
// failure and was silent. What AGENTS.md states is that the checker comes from
// the testing.TB the closure was handed, so that is what is asked.
package fixture

import (
	"testing"

	qt "github.com/frankban/quicktest"
)

type fixtureTB struct {
	tb testing.TB
}

func TestCheckerFromATBBoundByAnInitializer(t *testing.T) {
	parent := t

	t.Run("the checker is not built from the handed TB", func(t *testing.T) {
		c := qt.New(parent)
		c.Assert(1, qt.Equals, 1)
	})
}

func TestCheckerFromATBReachedThroughAField(t *testing.T) {
	held := fixtureTB{tb: t}

	t.Run("the checker is not built from the handed TB", func(t *testing.T) {
		c := qt.New(held.tb)
		c.Assert(2, qt.Equals, 2)
	})
}

// The target shape, and two things that are not violations: a helper closure
// nested inside the subtest builds its checker from the TB it was itself
// handed, and a subtest that asserts nothing needs no checker at all.
func TestConformingCheckerSources(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("the closure builds from its own parameter", func(t *testing.T) {
		c := qt.New(t)
		c.Assert(3, qt.Equals, 3)

		nested := func(tb testing.TB) {
			inner := qt.New(tb)
			inner.Assert(4, qt.Equals, 4)
		}
		nested(t)
	})

	t.Run("a subtest that asserts nothing needs no checker", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Log("work")
	})
}
